text:
Alex: Quick sync 1: Product asks if we can support per-route deprecation windows for v1 so internal services can stay on longer than public APIs. Can we do this without blowing up edge latency?

Maya: We currently only have org-level deprecation dates in rollout-service. No per-route key stored.

Sanjay: runtime does routing based on route-id and client version. Adding a route-level lookup is straightforward but we should avoid a DB roundtrip on hot paths.

Priya: UX: console needs to avoid banner spam. Proposal: single top-banner summarizing org state + expandable list of routes with deviating dates.

Alex: agree on summary + drilldown. Key engineering questions: how tenants set overrides, enforcement semantics, telemetry for unexpected evictions.

Maya: suggestion: add optional `deprecation_policy` field to the route config blob. The config distribution pipeline already pushes blobs to edge caches. No per-request DB hits.

Sanjay: perfect. Runtime will read cached blob at handshake and tag request with `deprecation_policy_source`. That adds zero DB latency. Need to ensure cache invalidation path when policy changes.

Priya: banner copy idea: "v1 deprecates for your org on 2026-06-01. 2 routes have custom windows (details)." Expand shows per-route countdowns and enforcement mode.

Alex: enforcement modes: notify/warn/throttle/force. For GA we should restrict tenant-facing modes to notify/warn; throttle/force requires infra-admins.

Maya: agree. Also need RBAC: tenants can only update policies for their routes. Add audit entry type `route.deprecation.update`.

Sanjay: telemetry signals requested: `route.deprecation.applied` (bool), `route.deprecation.source` (org/route/admin), and `route.deprecation.enforcement` (enum). Also a counter for `route.deprecation.override_reverts` so we can see churn.

Alex: add an SLO for false-positive evictions. If runtime flips clients unexpectedly we want alerts.

Priya: console UX details: when tenant sets a later date than org default show CTA: "This extends the org policy; infra may still enforce earlier org rules for shared tokens."

Maya: implementation plan:
1) schema: add `deprecation_policy` to route config proto (fields: date, mode, quota_pct)
2) console: editor + summary + audit log
3) config pipeline: write -> kafka -> config-distributor -> edge cache
4) runtime: consult cached route config, emit telemetry, enforce mode

Sanjay: sample proto (dev sketch):
```proto
message DeprecationPolicy {
  string deprecation_date = 1; // ISO8601
  enum Mode { NOTIFY = 0; WARN = 1; THROTTLE = 2; FORCE = 3; }
  Mode mode = 2;
  int32 quota_soft_pct = 3; // for THROTTLE
}
message RouteConfig {
  string route_id = 1;
  DeprecationPolicy deprecation = 10;
}
```

Alex: rollout: gate behind feature flag `route_deprecation_policy`. Canary to low-traffic tenants first. Deploy-bot: create flag and enable for cohort with <500 req/day.

deploy-bot: Feature flag `route_deprecation_policy` created. Cohort: traffic < 500 req/day. Enabled at 1788887960.

Maya: tests: precedence unit tests (route -> tenant -> org), integration tests for config distribution, and e2e for telemetry tags.

Priya: UX testcases: collapse/expand summary, conflict modal when tenant extends beyond org, and preview of per-route timelines.

Sanjay: billing question: if mode=THROTTLE do we apply token discounts? My vote: keep billing normal; throttle is purely rate-limiting, not discount. Finance can propose billing changes later.

Alex: noted. For now document that only FORCE might trigger billing adjustments and that remains infra-admin-only.

Maya: I'll add console mocks and api spec. Priya can review copy.

Priya: will do. Mock ETA: 48h.

Sanjay: runtime prototype ETA: 3 days. Will include cache invalidation integration.

Alex: thanks. We'll monitor canary metrics for 72h and iterate. Reopen thread for telemetry dashboards once data arrives.

deploy-bot: Canary enable logged at 1788887960. Metrics hooks: `deprecation_policy.applied`, `deprecation_policy.errors`, `config-distributor.latency`.
